headline: A controlled benchmark reports token-level fixes for language-model data attribution
summary: A preprint introduces the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT), which fine-tunes Qwen3.5-4B models on fictitious facts so the training documents provide known attribution ground truth. Across controlled settings, the authors report that redundancy and lexical distractors degrade gradient-based methods, while token-level negative log-odds gradients combined with top-k token aggregation improve fact-tracing recall by 35–72 percentage points. On FTRACE-TREX, the paper reports that negative log-odds improves counterfactual retraining performance for TRAK, EK-FAC and Grad-Dot by up to 4.9×. The tested tasks use single-token predictions and single-task LoRA fine-tuning; transfer to real pretraining attribution, multi-token outputs and multi-task learning remains unestablished.
